118385.name: Chabad of Encino
118385.note: Chabad of the Valley's own history (its About Us page, 2007): the Blauner Youth Center in Tarzana was dedicated 'on a fateful day in 1978 — five years into its existence', and 'At that time, Chabad of the Valley consisted of but a single center – a small house on Hayvenhurst Avenue in Encino – operated by Rabbi Gordon and his wife, Deborah' (this listing is at 4915 Hayvenhurst Ave). Rabbi Gordon's nephew's tribute (ChabadNewOrleans.com, 2016): 'He was the spiritual leader of Chabad of Encino, Rabbi and teacher to many at the Chabad House he and his wife Deborah founded in 1973, upon being sent by the Rebbe to the San Fernando Valley' (https://www.chabadneworleans.com/templates/blog/post_cdo/aid/1203266/postid/59034). Jewish Journal obituary (Feb 2016): spiritual leader of Chabad of Encino for more than 40 years.

117963.name: Blauner Youth Center
117963.note: Chabad of the Valley's own history (its About Us page, 2007): 'on a fateful day in 1978 — five years into its existence — ... Rabbi Joshua Gordon and a unique man named Jerry Blauner ... stood in front of a house on Burbank Boulevard in Tarzana and dedicated it as the "Israel and Anna Blauner Youth Center"'; its Gan Israel School opened there in 1978 with ten students; 'Two short years later, Rabbi Mordechai and Chave Einbinder would move to Tarzana be the spiritual leaders of the Tarzana center' (1980, therebbesimpact.com's year). Same dot as the Ryzman Family Hebrew School.

117545.name: Chabad of the Valley Headquarters
117545.note: Jewish Journal obituary (Feb 2016) of Rabbi Yehoshua B. Gordon, founder of Chabad of the Valley: 'Cunin recruited him to the West Coast in 1973'; the center's biography: 'his 43 years of leadership of Chabad of the Valley'. (therebbesimpact.com: 1980; a 2025 blog: 1979.)

earlier.where: a small house on Hayvenhurst Avenue, Encino (Chabad of the Valley's only center until the Blauner Youth Center in Tarzana opened in 1978; now Chabad of Encino)

117561.name: Chabad of Northridge
117561.note: Its '10 Year Anniversary Fund' page (June 2014) honors 'Rabbi Eli and Tzippy Rivkin for their 10 years of service to the community', so they came about 2004. The listing is in chabad.org's first directory (about 2003) and therebbesimpact.com gives 1988 for Chabad of Northridge itself, so the center may be older. Anash.org (Nov 12 2020, new shluchim to Northridge): the Rivkins 'have been directing Chabad activities in Northridge since 2004' (https://anash.org/new-shluchim-to-northridge-california/). No founding report found, and nothing yet on a Chabad in Northridge before them.
